status: secondary eyewitness reconstruction; physical-copy verification pending
central_claim: Multiple physical copies of Hodgson's 1874 Essays acquired divergent handwritten annotation histories. Edition identity therefore does not equal version identity.

source.citation: Harihar Raj Joshi and Indu Joshi, bibliography of Hodgson fugitive/extant materials, 2002

copies.layering: black ink sometimes written over earlier pencil annotation
copies.additional_material: annotated/corrected map of Nepal and Tibet
dating_evidence: annotation sequence begins by 1876 according to Joshi
copies.military_tribes_specific_page_reported: not specified in available page-list excerpt

copies.description: Joshi section 'Yet Another Annotated copy of Hodgson's Essays of 1874'

copies.inscription: To Mr. Townshend / with the affectionate regards of / the author / Alderley / Oct. 1. 1874
copies.later_provenance_note: Joshi reports presentation by the author's great-nephew in 1974

later_reprint_interface.description: 1972 Amsterdam reprint includes a Supplement of additions and corrections edited by Mahadeva Prasad Saha from handwritten annotations in the author's copy

graph_model: 1874 edition -> multiple copy-specific handwritten branches -> possible later editorial extraction/reprint
source_control_rules: Do not infer annotation content from page presence alone.
Do not merge the physical copies into one corrected-author text.
Joshi's provenance speculation about the copies' journey to Nepal is not established custody evidence.
Physically verify handwriting and page annotations before publication-level claims.
Identify the exact Saha source witness before connecting the 1972 supplement to any one copy branch.
next_actions: Recover Part II p.37 annotation in APB-ALDERLEY-OCT1874.
Locate full 1972 Saha supplement and search Part II pp.37-44.
